thread:
Noah: flagged an incident where client retries replayed whole streaming sessions and doubled GPU cost. want to discuss resume tokens + cross-node resume caching.
Ivy: ouch. we need a way to let a retried client continue from the last acked chunk instead of redoing the whole generation. resume token seems right.
Sam: agree. two concerns: token issuance/validation and cross-node lookup for canaries/dedicated pools.
Noah: propose server-issued opaque token (short-lived) that encodes route, model id, kv-checkpoint and offset. token stored in an in-memory LRU on the edge, optionally backed by per-region redis for cross-node resume. token TTL small (30-90s).
Rina: how to avoid state explosion? limit tokens per tenant and evict aggressively. issue token only after first stall/handshake or on explicit client request `resume=true`.
Kade: security: token should be HMAC-signed with ephemeral key so backends can verify without central lookup? or edge verifies and backend trusts edge via mTLS.
Ivy: I prefer edge-sign + backend trust via mTLS. keeps token validator simple and avoids DB hits on hot path. backends can skip lookup if they trust the edge header.
Sam: cross-node resume: if client retries to different edge node, we need token lookup. either: 1) embed enough checkpoint info in signed token to be stateless, or 2) replicate token to regional redis. embedding increases token size but no network hop.
Noah: embed minimal checkpoint (offset + model hash + kv-checkpoint-id) encrypted+signed. backend uses model hash to verify compatibility and applies the checkpoint to skip forward. redis option needed only if we want revocation.
Rina: we should support revoke-on-rollout: when we upgrade model we must invalidate tokens pointing to old model quickly. redis helps but embedding doesn't. maybe combine: embedded token + `token_id` optional replica for revocation list. on rollback/upgrade we add token_ids to revoke-set with short TTL.
Kade: good tradeoff. also consider storage cost for redis: we only store token_id->meta for tokens that opt into cross-node resume. default: embedded-only.
Sam: operational: we must surface metrics `resume_tokens_issued`, `resume_hits`, `resume_miss_due_to_model_mismatch`, `resume_revoked`. alert on resume_miss/model_mismatch > 1% of attempts.
Ivy: API + header: client receives resume token in response header `x-rw-resume-token`. on retry they send `x-rw-resume-token: <token>`. server responds `x-rw-resume-accepted: true|false` and `x-rw-resume-offset: N`.
Noah: config sketch (json):
{
  "route": "/v1/stream",
  "resume_policy": {
    "enabled": true,
    "embedded_token_ttl_s": 45,
    "replicated_token_ttl_s": 60,
    "max_tokens_per_tenant": 1000,
    "revoke_set_ttl_s": 120
  }
}
Sam: hedging interaction: hedging/parallel retries must be disabled when resume-token present. otherwise two hedged attempts might both accept the token and produce inconsistencies. we should treat resume-enabled requests as non-hedgeable.
Rina: also note billing: if resume reduces duplicate computation, cost per-request drops. update accounting to credit partial replays appropriately and log when resumed so billing is accurate.
Kade: failure modes: if model mismatch on resume, return 409 + `resume_model_mismatch` and suggest client drop token and retry fresh. if token expired -> 410. if token revoked -> 403.
Ivy: rollout: feature flag `edge.resume_tokens_v1`. start with dedicated internal models only, canary 0.5% external. create chaos test that forces node flip during resume.
Noah: owners: Sam gateway impl + embed/encrypt logic, Rina token lifecycle + redis revocation, Ivy SDK + header docs, Kade security review, I'll draft RFC with sequence diagrams and failure flows.
